text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every case contained exactly one of three alternative activities between A39 and A24: A14 in about 35 in 100 traces, A15 in about 30, A16 in about 36 (the three shares cover all traces, no two of the three ever occurred in the same trace, and each appeared at most once per trace). In the later window, none of A14, A15 or A16 appears in any of the 200 traces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, REL001, REL002, REL008, DIR007]

- In the later window, A21, A22 and A23 — absent from all 200 earlier traces — each run exactly once in every trace (participation and mean occurrences per trace both 1.0, no repetitions). [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]

- In the later window the three new activities always occur together, and their pairwise order is mixed rather than fixed: A21 precedes A22 in about 51 in 100 cases and follows it in about 49, with similar near-even splits for A21–A23 (about 51/49) and A22–A23 (about 52/48). In the earlier window these pairs never occurred in the same trace. [REL019, REL020, REL023]

- The surrounding frame is unchanged: A39 and A24 occur in every trace in both windows. Earlier, A39 led directly into A14/A15/A16 (about 35/30/36 of its outgoing transitions) and each of those led to A24 in every one of its uses; in the later window A39 leads into A21/A22/A23 (about 36/33/32), each new activity precedes A24 in all 200 traces, and each also connects directly to A24 in roughly one third of its outgoing transitions — consistent with the three running one after another in varying order before A24. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, REL021, REL022, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027]

- Event positions (not clock time) agree with this picture: the old three sat at a mean relative position of about 0.36, the new three at about 0.37, and A24's mean position moved slightly later, from about 0.39 to about 0.44, as expected when three activities now sit between A39 and A24 instead of one. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the segment between A39 and A24 was restructured: in the earlier window each case ran A39, then exactly one of A14, A15 or A16, then A24, whereas in the later window each case runs A39, then A21, A22 and A23 — all three, once each, in varying order with no fixed sequence among them — then A24. The change is shown directly by participation flipping from about 35/30/36 in 100 traces to zero for the old three, and from zero to 200 in 200 for the new three; by co-occurrence flipping from mutually exclusive alternatives to universal co-occurrence with mixed internal order; and by A39's outgoing edges and the edges into A24 redirecting to the new activities. The screening context makes chance an unlikely explanation for the pattern as a whole: 47 control-flow items qualified where about 0.5 would be expected if nothing had changed, and every item ranks above about 995 in 1000 random re-splits. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL001, REL002, REL008, REL019, REL020, REL023, REL021, REL022, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]

The many qualifying items largely restate this one underlying difference rather than providing independent confirmations. Two competing explanations cannot be ruled out: the windows may capture two coexisting process variants whose shares flipped between the windows (a variant present in fewer than roughly 1 in 200 earlier cases would go unseen in this sample), and the evidence cannot show whether A21/A22/A23 are relabelled counterparts of A14/A15/A16 or genuinely different activities. [OCC001, OCC004, REL019]
